site_selection_index_test: All patients presenting with symptoms and signs suggestive of oral premalignant lesions and suspected oral malignancy; lesions most frequently on the buccal mucosa and lateral border of the tongue.
technique: Mouth rinsed with water for 20 s to remove debris; 1% acetic acid applied for 20 s to remove ropey saliva; 1% toluidine blue oral rinse given for 20 s; 1% acetic acid rinse repeated to remove mechanically retained stain; mouth rinsed with water.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that exhibited dark blue staining were deemed positive for premalignant or malignant tissue, while those with light staining or no color were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain retention
blinding_index_test_assessors: The pathologists who examined the biopsies were not informed about the clinical or staining evaluations of the samples.
comments_index_test: The figure caption states '0.1% solution' but the methods consistently describe a '1% solution of modified toluidine blue'. Unit of analysis is patients. The reference standard (HPE) was applied to all lesions including TB-negative ones that did not resolve, but the paper does not clarify whether all 100 patients received biopsy or only a subset.

site_selection_index_test: Applied over the oral lesion with a cotton swab, covering approximately 2 cm margin all around the lesion
technique: Mouth rinsed with water to remove debris; 1% Acetic Acid rinse for 20 s to remove saliva; area dried with gauze; 1% Toluidine Blue applied with cotton swab for 1 min covering ~2 cm margin around lesion; 1% Acetic Acid rinse for 1 min; dye uptake pattern observed under proper light.
positivity_threshold: A stain was considered as positive for malignancy if the lesion diffusely or partly stained dark blue (royal or navy blue), or had stippled appearance. All equivocal lesions were considered positively stained unless proved otherwise.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue (royal or navy blue) or stippled stain retention
calibration_of_assessors: The clinical examination was done by a single expert otorhinolaryngologist; wedge biopsy done by a single surgeon in all cases.
blinding_index_test_assessors: The pathologists examining the biopsy specimens were not informed regarding the staining information of the samples.
comments_index_test: Study has two arms: Group A (conventional biopsy by clinical judgment, n=100) and Group B (Toluidine Blue staining prior to biopsy, n=100). Only Group B is the index test arm. Alternate sampling used rather than true randomization, which the authors acknowledge as a limitation. The comparator arm (Group A, clinical suspicion only) is not an index test arm per se but is compared for diagnostic accuracy.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspected oral lesions identified on routine clinical examination; sites included buccal mucosa, tongue, alveolar mucosa, palate, and lip.
technique: Participants rinsed with solution B (purified water, raspberry flavor, 1% lactic acid) for 20 seconds; mucosa was dried with triple syringe and gauze; solution A (1% methylene blue) applied; after 20-second wait, patients rinsed again with solution B for 20 seconds; stain intensity noted after rinse. Deep blue stains = positive; faint/wide blue stains = negative. Cotton rolls used to apply solution B to clear stained surface; retained stain recorded as positive.
positivity_threshold: Local, stippled and concentrated (deep) blue stains indicate a positive reaction; wide and faint blue stains indicate a negative reaction. If stain retained after rinsing with solution B, positive result was recorded.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: deep/concentrated blue stain retention after rinse
comments_index_test: Single-arm study with one observer recording stain intensity. No precancerous lesions were found in the sample (all histopathology results were either malignant or benign), limiting generalisability to premalignant lesions. The reference standard (biopsy) was guided by the site of maximum dye uptake, which may introduce incorporation bias.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to conspicuous oral lesions with apparent variation from normal healthy mucosa
specimen_collection: Five brush smears per lesion taken with nylon brush, brush head placed tangentially to oral lesion and rotated at least ten times, then head washed out in preservation vial
technique: Five smears per lesion pooled in one SurePath™ vial; brush head rotated ≥10 times against lesion then washed into fixative; cells deposited by gravitational force and transferred to glass slides; stained by Papanicolaou (PAP); evaluated using German classification for extragenital cytology (Böcking et al.)
positivity_threshold: 'Doubtful', 'suspicious' and 'positive' cytological results were overall considered as positive for malignancy; only 'negative' was reported as 'tumour cell negative'
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: doubtful, suspicious, or positive cytology result
comments_index_test: Five brush smears per lesion were pooled into a single SurePath™ vial for the nylon brush arm, compared to one smear for the rigid brush arm; this procedural difference may affect diagnostic accuracy. Study is retrospective and consecutive; patients from January 2009 to May 2012.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to conspicuous oral lesions with apparent variation from normal healthy mucosa
specimen_collection: One brush smear per lesion taken with rigid brush; brush head placed tangentially to oral lesion and rotated at least ten times, then head washed out in preservation vial
technique: Single obtainment per lesion; brush head rotated ≥10 times against lesion then washed into SurePath™ vial; cells deposited by gravitational force and transferred to glass slides; stained by Papanicolaou (PAP); evaluated using German classification for extragenital cytology (Böcking et al.)
positivity_threshold: 'Doubtful', 'suspicious' and 'positive' cytological results were overall considered as positive for malignancy; only 'negative' was reported as 'tumour cell negative'
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: doubtful, suspicious, or positive cytology result
comments_index_test: Single brush smear per lesion for rigid brush arm vs. five smears for nylon brush arm; this procedural difference likely contributes to the observed difference in specificity. Study is retrospective and consecutive; patients from June 2012 to February 2018. Rigid brush showed lower specificity (84.9%) than nylon brush (94.2%), attributed in part to higher rate of 'doubtful' results.

site_selection_index_test: Lesional and perilesional tissue of suspicious oral lesions was assessed during direct visual fluorescent examination.
technique: Direct visual fluorescent examination was performed using VELscope VX handpiece. Lesional and perilesional tissue was assessed for visual fluorescence retention (VFR) and visual fluorescence loss (VFL). Digital photographs of tissue fluorescence were acquired through the VELscope viewing handpiece using iPod 5 digital camera connected to VELscope by image adapter.
positivity_threshold: Visual fluorescence loss (VFL) — appearance of a black area detected as fluorescence visualization loss — classified as positive; visual fluorescence retention (VFR) classified as negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss (VFL)
comments_index_test: Single-arm study. VELscope examination preceded biopsy/histopathology; biopsy site was chosen to cover both COE and VEL positive regions. Sensitivity 76.92%, specificity 64.86%, PPV 43.48%, NPV 88.88%. Study appears to be the first of its kind conducted in Iraq.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
technique: A cotton bud soaked in 1% acetic acid was used to clean the lesion prior to the application of toluidine blue with a different cotton tip for 30 s. Subsequently, a third cotton bud soaked with 1% acetic acid was used to remove any excess toluidine blue on the lesion. The patient then rinsed out their mouth.
positivity_threshold: A positive lesion was the one which color changed to blue, while a negative lesion was with no change.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: stain retention (color changed to blue)
comments_index_test: 33 patients received toluidine blue alone; an additional 24 patients received both toluidine blue and vinegar (reported in a separate arm). Analysis for p53 IHC was performed on specimens from toluidine blue arms only (excluding the 24 combined-arm patients). Note that 67 lesions came from only 54 patients, indicating some patients had multiple lesions.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
technique: A gauze soaked with vinegar was applied to a clean and dry lesion for one minute. The researcher noted the changes and took picture of the lesion. An incisional biopsy was performed at the area that had turned opaque white.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was designated when a lesion changed to opaque white. When a lesion did not change or changed to transparent white, a negative finding was indicated.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: lesion changed to opaque white
comments_index_test: 30 patients received vinegar alone; an additional 24 patients received both vinegar and toluidine blue (reported in a separate arm). Ki67 IHC analysis was performed on vinegar-arm specimens only (excluding the 24 combined-arm patients). 83 lesions from 57 patients, indicating some patients had multiple lesions.

site_selection_index_test: An oral medicine specialist recorded clinical findings, took pictures of the lesions, and picked the areas to be examined.
technique: Application of vinegar was conducted first, followed by the application of toluidine blue. A positive finding was indicated for a lesion with color changed to both opaque white and blue. An incisional biopsy was performed at the area that turned opaque white and had stained blue. If the areas did not coincide, biopsies were performed at both areas.
positivity_threshold: A positive finding was indicated for a lesion with color changed to both opaque white and blue, while a negative finding was a lesion not demonstrating these combined changes.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: lesion changed to both opaque white and blue
comments_index_test: Tissues from these 24 patients were not included in the immunohistochemical analysis (p53 or Ki67). There is a discrepancy: the text states '27 lesions' while the table title states '28 specimens from 24 patients'; this may reflect one lesion requiring two biopsies.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to oral mucosal lesions in all patients presenting with clinical features suggestive of OPMDs (oral leukoplakia/oral erythroplakia, OLPs/OLLs, or OSCCs)
specimen_collection: OLBC using Orcellex brush performed on each patient under local anesthesia before undergoing surgical biopsy; brush heads preserved immediately into vials of methanol-based buffered preservative
technique: Brush heads preserved in methanol-based buffered preservative (ThinPrep PreservCyt); LBC slide automatically prepared using ThinPrep 2000 processor; slides Papanicolaou-stained using ThinPrep staining reagents per manufacturer protocol; slides blindly and independently assessed by three assessors using modified 2014 Bethesda system; discrepancies settled by consensus
positivity_threshold: Cytological findings categorized into five groups: (1) atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance; (2) atypical squamous cells suggestive of OLP or lichenoid reaction; (3) low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion; (4) high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion; (5) OSCC. Positive defined as low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, or OSCC (categories 3–5).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: low-grade SIL, high-grade SIL, or OSCC on modified 2014 Bethesda system
calibration_of_assessors: Three assessors (M.I., O.K., P.S.) independently assessed all slides; discrepancies settled by consensus
blinding_index_test_assessors: LBC slides were assessed blindly (blinded to histopathological diagnosis)
comments_index_test: 31 patients (9.8%) excluded due to inadequate cellularity; unit of analysis is patients not lesions; prevalence of positive cases (OED low/high risk + OSCC) stated as 101/284 in Table 1 footnote; cost-utility analysis also performed comparing OLBC with surgical biopsy using Australian Medicare Benefits Schedule.

site_selection_index_test: The main site of morphologically altered mucosa was selected and photographed before TB staining was applied.
technique: 1% TB applied in 4 steps: (1) rinse oral cavity with water for 20 s to remove debris; (2) application/rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s; (3) application/rinse with TB solution (1% W/W) for 20 s; (4) application/rinse with 1% acetic acid for 20 s to eliminate mechanically retained stains.
positivity_threshold: A royal blue or a navy blue stain was considered as a positive result even if either the entire lesion or a portion of the lesion is stained or stippled. A light blue staining is considered doubtful. If there is no colour absorbed by the lesion, it was taken as a negative stain.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: royal blue or navy blue stain retention (whole or partial lesion)
calibration_of_assessors: Dental surgeons in the selected institutions were trained by the expert in the field of Oral Medicine at their institutions. Live demonstrations of TB application were carried out to familiarise the procedure during the training programme.
comments_index_test: Five patients received TB test but were excluded from the validity analysis due to missing histopathological data (65 received vs 60 analyzed). No control group was included. Study acknowledged subjectivity in interpreting intermediate/faintly positive staining as a limitation.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspicious lesions in the oral cavity; sites included buccal mucosa, tongue, gums, floor of mouth, and lip.
technique: 1) Clinically suspicious lesion areas applied with 1% acetic acid using cotton bud for 20 seconds, repeated once, then rinsed with water. 2) Toluidine blue applied with cotton bud for 10–20 seconds. 3) Lesion decolorized with 2% acetic acid using cotton bud for 20–30 seconds, then photograph taken.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue was considered as positive for lesions suspicious of malignancy, light blue retention was considered as positive for premalignant lesions unless proved otherwise by biopsy, and lesion without retention was considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: stain retention (dark or light blue); negative: no retention
comments_index_test: The staining protocol includes a pre-wash with 1% acetic acid and decolorization with 2% acetic acid. No waiting period for inflammatory lesion resolution was used (unlike Mashberg), which authors acknowledge may affect specificity. Biopsy was obtained from all subjects both before and after staining for histopathological reference standard.

index_test_reagent_name: BD SurePath liquid-based cytology with Orcellex® Brush
site_selection_index_test: Patients with clearly visible oral lesions showing apparent variation from normal healthy mucosa; sites included tongue, gingiva, floor of the mouth, buccal mucosa, palatal plate, and lips.
specimen_collection: Cell samples collected using the Orcellex® Brush by twisting the brush ten times; the head of the cell collector was then transferred directly into an alcohol-based liquid in the BD SurePath™ Collection Vial.
technique: Cells were spread in a fixative solution to create a thin layer on the slide; stained with Papanicolaou stain according to standard procedure; assessed using modified 2014 Bethesda Cervical Cytology grading system including cellularity, quality of preparation, cell types, microbiota, leucocytes, artifacts, and dyskeratotic/SCC features.
positivity_threshold: Positive: malignant cells observed; Doubtful: malignant cells suspected but not confirmed; Negative: no atypical cells observed in the smear. For analysis, cytology positive = doubtful + positive.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: malignant or suspected malignant cells observed (doubtful or positive categories)
calibration_of_assessors: All participating experts had passed the board examination of the Japanese Society of Pathology for oral pathology and had been practicing for >7 years; discrepancies settled by consensus.
comments_index_test: Single-centre retrospective study. Two patients had inadequate material and were excluded from the 2×2 contingency table analysis (651 patients used). Sensitivity 69%, specificity 75%, PPV 38%, NPV 92%. Doubtful and positive categories combined as 'positive' for sensitivity/specificity calculations.

index_test_reagent_name: Direct fluorescence visualization device; excitation filter 425 nm (60 nm bandpass); emission filter 475 nm long-pass
site_selection_index_test: After turning off the room light, the oral cavity was viewed with direct FV.
technique: Blue excitation light (400–460 nm) projected onto oral mucosa via handheld unit with coaxial excitation and emission pathways. Tissue fluorescence viewed directly through a viewing port. FV retention (FVR) classified as lesions retaining normal pale green autofluorescence; FV loss (FVL) classified as distinct reduction to dark green or black, compared with adjacent tissue and contralateral anatomical control.
positivity_threshold: FV loss (FVL): tissue showing a distinct reduction in the normal pale green autofluorescence, appearing as dark green to black
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss (dark green to black appearance)
comments_index_test: Pilot study; unit of analysis is lesions (biopsies), not patients. Clinicians decided biopsy based on standard clinical features and toluidine blue staining, not direct FV, so FV assessment was not part of clinical decision-making. Only severe dysplasia/CIS and invasive SCC were compared to normal — mild and moderate dysplasia lesions appear not to have been included or separately analyzed. Photographs were taken for documentation only and not used for classification.

index_test_reagent_name: hBD-2 and hBD-3 ELISA (sandwich ELISA with hBD-2 and hBD-3 antibody pairs; cell lysates from cytobrush samples)
index_test_commercial_name: Defensin 2, beta (Human) - ELISA Kit (Cat#EK-072-52); Defensin 3, beta (Human) - ELISA Kit (Cat#EK-072-38) [external validation]; Rovers Orcellex Brush RT [cytobrush]
site_selection_index_test: Applied to a visible, accessible suspicious oral lesion (red or white lesion present ≥2 weeks in the same location) and to the contralateral normal oral mucosa of the same patient.
specimen_collection: Cytobrush (Rovers Orcellex Brush) applied with pressure and rotated 10 turns to collect cells from the full thickness of the lesion; brush placed in 2 mL PBS collection tube on ice; same procedure repeated at contralateral normal site.
technique: Paired cytobrush samples from lesion and contralateral normal site collected and stored at -80°C. Cells dislodged from brush, centrifuged, and lysed in RIPA buffer. Cell lysates assayed by sandwich ELISA for hBD-2 and hBD-3. BDI = [OD_hBD-3/OD_hBD-2]_lesion / [OD_hBD-3/OD_hBD-2]_contralateral normal.
positivity_threshold: BDI ≥ 1.25 indicates cancer (positive); arrived at a BDI cutoff value of 1.25 and found 100% sensitivity with an acceptable specificity value of 80%.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: BDI ≥ 1.25
calibration_of_assessors: To avoid inter-operator variability, the same clinician collected paired cytobrush samples in the discovery phase. One laboratory operator generated BDI values in the discovery and internal validation phases. Samples were intentionally blinded so pathologist-determined diagnoses were revealed only after BDI scores were obtained.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Yes — samples were intentionally blinded so that pathologist-determined diagnoses were revealed only after BDI scores were obtained for all patients in both discovery and validation phases.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the paper does not explicitly state whether the clinician collecting cytobrush samples was blinded to clinical information beyond the lesion being suspicious; blinding of the laboratory operator to clinical information other than the reference standard is not described.
comments_index_test: This is a multi-phase study: proof-of-concept (n=8), discovery (n=40), and three validation cohorts (internal n=21; external 1 n=19; external 2 n=12), totalling 92 subjects analysed (100 enrolled). The index test is a novel ratio biomarker (BDI) derived from cytobrush ELISA, not a conventional cytology stain; it is categorised here as 'Cytology' because the specimen collection is cytological (exfoliated mucosal cells via cytobrush). External validation cohorts used Phoenix Pharmaceuticals ELISA kits rather than the in-house Peprotech sandwich ELISA. A separate MICA (microfluidic intact cell assay) proof-of-concept arm (n=5 OSCC + 5 healthy) is described but uses intact cells with fluorescent antibodies, not ELISA; it is not included in the primary sensitivity/specificity table and is a separate sub-study.

index_test_arm_label: Cytology (Beta-defensin Index MICA - microfluidic intact cell assay)
index_test_reagent_name: Anti-hBD-3 (Alexa Fluor 488 conjugated) and anti-hBD-2 (Alexa Fluor 647 conjugated) fluorescent antibodies; cells permeabilized with 0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS; MICA microfluidic chip with polydimethylsiloxane micropillar arrays
index_test_commercial_name: MICA (microfluidic intact cell assay) — investigational device; Rovers Orcellex Brush RT for specimen collection
site_selection_index_test: Cytobrush samples collected from OSCC lesional sites and contralateral normal sites of 5 OSCC patients, and from left and right cheek (or tongue) of 5 healthy subjects.
specimen_collection: Cytobrush samples collected in PBS and added to EDTA-containing vacutainer tubes to prevent coagulation; processed within 2–3 h post collection to maintain intact cells.
technique: Cytobrush cells injected into MICA microchannel (PDMS micropillar arrays, openings 160–20 µm) under 40 mbar pressure; fixed with 4% formaldehyde; permeabilized with 0.1% Triton X-100; stained with DAPI plus anti-hBD-3 (AF488) and anti-hBD-2 (AF647) antibodies; imaged under 10× objective; BDI = [hBD-3 pixel/hBD-2 pixel]L / [hBD-3 pixel/hBD-2 pixel]N.
positivity_threshold: Higher BDI in OSCC lesions compared to healthy/contralateral tissue; same BDI formula (hBD-3/hBD-2 ratio of lesional over contralateral) applied; specific numeric cutoff not re-stated for MICA arm.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: higher BDI (hBD-3/hBD-2 ratio lesion > contralateral)
calibration_of_assessors: NR — no specific calibration or training of MICA assessors is described beyond the image segmentation protocol using a pre-trained deep learning model.
blinding_index_test_assessors: NR — blinding of MICA assessors to histopathological reference standard is not explicitly stated for this proof-of-concept sub-study.
blinding_index_test_examiner: NR — the paper does not report whether MICA examiners were blinded to clinical information for this sub-study.
comments_index_test: This is a proof-of-concept sub-study (n=5 OSCC + 5 healthy) for MICA and does not contribute to the primary sensitivity/specificity data in Table 1. Healthy subjects (not patients with suspicious lesions) were used as the comparator group, unlike the ELISA BDI arm which compared OSCC vs. benign lesion patients. No formal diagnostic accuracy metrics (sensitivity/specificity) are reported for this arm. This arm should be excluded from any meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy.

index_test_reagent_name: Feulgen-thionin staining for DNA image cytometry
index_test_commercial_name: GEMINI Medical Diagnostic System's (Changsha) DNA Image Cytometer (DNA-ICM)
site_selection_index_test: Brush samples obtained from oral mucosal lesions (OLK, OSF, or OSF+OLK) at the same site as the incisional biopsy.
specimen_collection: The clinician instructs the patient to rinse the mouth with water and then gently scrape the oral mucosal lesions at least 10 times using the flexible cotton cytology brush; brush head stored in cell preservation solution and sent within 24 hours.
technique: Samples processed as liquid-based thin-layer cell preparation and Feulgen-thionin stained; slides scanned with DNA Image Cytometer; DNA quantitative analysis performed when specimens contained at least 300 epithelial cell nuclei normalized to normal epithelial cell nuclei; DNA index (DI) calculated as ratio of sample nuclei DNA content to reference normal nuclear DNA content.
positivity_threshold: Abnormal DNA content: aneuploid group >3 nuclei (1% of at least 300 nuclei) with DNA index ≥2.3, OR hyperdiploid group ≥5% of total nuclei (1.25 ≤ DI ≤ 1.75), OR tetraploid group ≥10% of total nuclei (1.25 ≤ DI ≤ 2.3).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: abnormal DNA content (aneuploidy, hyperdiploidy, or tetraploidy thresholds met)
blinding_index_test_assessors: DNA image cytometry was performed blinded to the histological results.
comments_index_test: Study includes three disease subgroups (OSF, OLK, OSF+OLK) analyzed within a single DNA-ICM arm; sensitivity and specificity reported separately per subgroup and per dysplasia grade. Cotton brushes used may have reduced accuracy. Cross-sectional design limits longitudinal inference.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (VelScope) - Unskilled General Dentist
site_selection_index_test: Applied to oral lesions in patients with OPMDs (leukoplakia, erythroplakia, oral lichen planus, lichenoid lesions, unspecified keratotic lesions); device held approximately 5 cm from oral cavity.
technique: Device held approximately 5 cm from oral cavity to optimize visualization of natural tissue fluorescence; operating theatre darkened if necessary to reduce natural light. Loss of autofluorescence (LAF) interpreted as positive result.
positivity_threshold: Presence of loss of autofluorescence (LAF) — darker aspects in comparison with surrounding areas; LAF defines the Vel-E as positive.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (LAF)
calibration_of_assessors: The unskilled general dentist had no prior training; the skilled general dentist underwent a 1-year post-graduate oral medicine training program at the Oral Medicine Unit, Federico II University of Naples.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Both examiners classified lesions based on clinical information and in the absence of histological data.
comments_index_test: This arm corresponds to the unskilled general dentist (u-GD) performing VelScope examination. The study has two parallel index-test arms (u-GD and s-GD) applied to the same 35 patients. The reference standard (biopsy) assessor was blinded to Vel-E results. Small sample size (n=35) acknowledged as limitation by authors.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (VelScope) - Skilled General Dentist
site_selection_index_test: Applied to oral lesions in patients with OPMDs (leukoplakia, erythroplakia, oral lichen planus, lichenoid lesions, unspecified keratotic lesions); device held approximately 5 cm from oral cavity.
technique: Device held approximately 5 cm from oral cavity to optimize visualization of natural tissue fluorescence; operating theatre darkened if necessary to reduce natural light. Loss of autofluorescence (LAF) interpreted as positive result.
positivity_threshold: Presence of loss of autofluorescence (LAF) — darker aspects in comparison with surrounding areas; LAF defines the Vel-E as positive.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (LAF)
calibration_of_assessors: The skilled general dentist underwent a 1-year post-graduate oral medicine training program at the Oral Medicine Unit, Federico II University of Naples, Italy, before performing the study examinations.
blinding_index_test_assessors: Both examiners classified lesions based on clinical information and in the absence of histological data.
comments_index_test: This arm corresponds to the skilled general dentist (s-GD) performing VelScope examination after 1-year oral medicine training. The same 35 patients were examined by both u-GD and s-GD arms, so arms are not independent. Reference standard assessor (oral pathologist) was blinded to Vel-E results. Small sample size acknowledged as limitation.

index_test_reagent_name: Modified brush cytology using commercially available toothbrush (medium bristles)
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions; most common site was buccal mucosa (74.07%), followed by tongue, hard palate, and lower alveolar region.
specimen_collection: Material obtained from the brush was deposited onto a glass slide; for cytocentrifugation the brush material was immersed in 15 mL normal saline.
technique: Patients instructed to rinse oral cavity with normal saline before procedure. Commercially available toothbrush (medium bristles) used to obtain material. Material deposited onto a glass slide. H&E, PAP, and MGG stained smears prepared; H&E and PAP smears fixed with isopropyl alcohol; MGG smears air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized according to the oral Bethesda system into NILM, LSIL, HSIL, and SCC; positive indicates LSIL, HSIL, or SCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LSIL, HSIL, or SCC by oral Bethesda system
comments_index_test: Study compares four cytology techniques (BR, BRCC, SR, SRCC) in the same 27 patients; lesion-level analysis not reported; 23/27 had histopathology for concordance. Low specificity (50%) attributed to small sample size.

index_test_reagent_name: Brush cytology cytocentrifugation using toothbrush material in 15 mL normal saline, cytocentrifuged at 1250 rpm for 3 min (program No. 1)
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions; most common site was buccal mucosa (74.07%), followed by tongue, hard palate, and lower alveolar region.
specimen_collection: Material obtained from BR technique immersed in 15 mL normal saline solution, mixed well and subjected to cytocentrifugation.
technique: Material from BR technique immersed in normal saline (15 mL), mixed well, cytocentrifuged at 1250 rpm for 3 min (program No. 1). H&E, PAP, and MGG stained smears prepared; H&E and PAP smears fixed with isopropyl alcohol; MGG smears air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized according to the oral Bethesda system into NILM, LSIL, HSIL, and SCC; positive indicates LSIL, HSIL, or SCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LSIL, HSIL, or SCC by oral Bethesda system
comments_index_test: BRCC is the novel indigenous liquid-based variant of BR using only normal saline as processing fluid. Same 27 patients received all four techniques. BRCC showed highest overall performance score (mean 20.37). 23/27 had histopathology available.

index_test_reagent_name: Modified scrape cytology using commercially available plastic ice cream spoon
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions; most common site was buccal mucosa (74.07%), followed by tongue, hard palate, and lower alveolar region.
specimen_collection: Material scraped using plastic ice cream spoon and deposited onto a glass slide; for cytocentrifugation the material was immersed in 15 mL normal saline.
technique: Patients instructed to rinse oral cavity with normal saline before procedure. Plastic ice cream spoon used to scrape material. Material deposited onto glass slide. H&E, PAP, and MGG stained smears prepared; H&E and PAP smears fixed with isopropyl alcohol; MGG smears air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized according to the oral Bethesda system into NILM, LSIL, HSIL, and SCC; positive indicates LSIL, HSIL, or SCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LSIL, HSIL, or SCC by oral Bethesda system
comments_index_test: SR technique failed to provide diagnosis in 2/27 cases (one adenoid cystic carcinoma showed only hemorrhagic material). Showed lowest overall performance (mean 13.96). Same 27 patients received all four techniques.

index_test_reagent_name: Scrape cytology cytocentrifugation using plastic ice cream spoon material in 15 mL normal saline, cytocentrifuged at 1250 rpm for 3 min (program No. 1)
site_selection_index_test: Clinically suspected potentially malignant and malignant oral cavity lesions; most common site was buccal mucosa (74.07%), followed by tongue, hard palate, and lower alveolar region.
specimen_collection: Material from SR technique immersed in 15 mL normal saline solution, mixed well and subjected to cytocentrifugation.
technique: Material from SR (plastic ice cream spoon scrape) technique immersed in normal saline (15 mL), mixed well, cytocentrifuged at 1250 rpm for 3 min (program No. 1). H&E, PAP, and MGG stained smears prepared; H&E and PAP smears fixed with isopropyl alcohol; MGG smears air-dried.
positivity_threshold: Lesions categorized according to the oral Bethesda system into NILM, LSIL, HSIL, and SCC; positive indicates LSIL, HSIL, or SCC.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: LSIL, HSIL, or SCC by oral Bethesda system
comments_index_test: SRCC failed to provide diagnosis in 1/27 cases. Showed better concordance than SR (95.45% vs 95.24%). Same 27 patients received all four techniques. Overall performance mean 18.93, second to BRCC.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Tissue reflectance (Reid's Colposcopic Index)
index_test_reagent_name: 5% acetic acid and 1% iodine Lugol's iodine solution (1% iodine, 2% potassium iodide, 97% distilled water)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to oral lesions (oral leukoplakia and oral lichen planus) on buccal mucosa, tongue, floor of mouth, and palate
technique: After wiping mucosa with saline, green filter used to view vascular patterns at high magnification (≥×30); 5% acetic acid applied for ~60 seconds to assess aceto-whitening at low magnification (≤×20); then Lugol's solution applied to assess iodine intake score at low magnification (≤×20). Scored using RCI with cutoff value of 5 to segregate dysplastic from nondysplastic lesions.
positivity_threshold: Cutoff value of 5 according to the RCI to segregate dysplastic lesions from nondysplastic lesions
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: RCI score ≥5
calibration_of_assessors: The colposcopic score for each participant was done by 2 assessors independently
