technique: Image processing analysis performed on FV images using ImageJ. ROIs for lesion and control area established. MeanV (mean G value) extracted from lesion ROI. Cut-off set at 52.5.
positivity_threshold: Cut-off set at MeanV 52.5; values below cut-off considered positive for oral cancer.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: mean G value below 52.5
comments_index_test: Objective evaluation sub-arm using mean G value (MeanV). AUC 0.651, sensitivity 43.7%, specificity 84.6%. Part of multi-parameter image analysis; shares patient population with all other objective evaluation arms.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (Fluorescence Visualization - Objective Evaluation: Median Green Value)
index_test_reagent_name: Blue light excitation at approximately 422 nm (ORALOOK) / 425 nm (IllumiScan); median G value (MediV) computed by image processing analysis in ImageJ
index_test_commercial_name: ORALOOK® (HITS PLAN, Tokyo, Japan); IllumiScan® (SHOFU, Kyoto, Japan)
site_selection_index_test: ROI of lesion defined as area of FVL; control ROI set at normal mucosa in same sub-site, away from lesion without FVL.
technique: Image processing analysis performed on FV images using ImageJ. ROIs for lesion and control area established. MediV (median G value) extracted from lesion ROI. Cut-off set at 60.0.
positivity_threshold: Cut-off set at MediV 60.0; values below cut-off considered positive for oral cancer.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: median G value below 60.0
comments_index_test: Objective evaluation sub-arm using median G value (MediV). AUC 0.633, sensitivity 55.2%, specificity 67.0%. Shares patient population with all other objective evaluation arms.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (Fluorescence Visualization - Objective Evaluation: Coefficient of Variation of Green Value)
index_test_reagent_name: Blue light excitation at approximately 422 nm (ORALOOK) / 425 nm (IllumiScan); coefficient of variation of G value (CV) computed by image processing analysis in ImageJ
index_test_commercial_name: ORALOOK® (HITS PLAN, Tokyo, Japan); IllumiScan® (SHOFU, Kyoto, Japan)
site_selection_index_test: ROI of lesion defined as area of FVL; control ROI set at normal mucosa in same sub-site, away from lesion without FVL.
technique: Image processing analysis performed on FV images using ImageJ. ROIs for lesion and control area established. CV (coefficient of variation of G value) extracted from lesion ROI. Cut-off set at 0.15.
positivity_threshold: Cut-off set at CV 0.15; values above cut-off considered positive for oral cancer.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: coefficient of variation of G value above 0.15
comments_index_test: Objective evaluation sub-arm using coefficient of variation (CV) of G value. AUC 0.820, sensitivity 82.1% (paper also reports 82.0% in abstract), specificity 69.4% (abstract reports 44.2% — discrepancy between abstract and Table 2). Shares patient population with all other objective evaluation arms.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (Fluorescence Visualization - Objective Evaluation: Skewness)
index_test_reagent_name: Blue light excitation at approximately 422 nm (ORALOOK) / 425 nm (IllumiScan); skewness of G value distribution computed by image processing analysis in ImageJ
index_test_commercial_name: ORALOOK® (HITS PLAN, Tokyo, Japan); IllumiScan® (SHOFU, Kyoto, Japan)
site_selection_index_test: ROI of lesion defined as area of FVL; control ROI set at normal mucosa in same sub-site, away from lesion without FVL.
technique: Image processing analysis performed on FV images using ImageJ. ROIs for lesion and control area established. Skewness of G value distribution extracted from lesion ROI. Cut-off set at 0.71.
positivity_threshold: Cut-off set at skewness 0.71; values above cut-off considered positive for oral cancer.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: skewness of G value above 0.71
comments_index_test: Objective evaluation sub-arm using skewness of G value. AUC 0.651, sensitivity 59.6%; specificity reported as 45.3% in abstract but 63.0% in Table 2 — discrepancy noted. Shares patient population with all other objective evaluation arms.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (Fluorescence Visualization - Objective Evaluation: Value Ratio)
index_test_reagent_name: Blue light excitation at approximately 422 nm (ORALOOK) / 425 nm (IllumiScan); value ratio (VRatio = lesion G value / control G value) computed by image processing analysis in ImageJ
index_test_commercial_name: ORALOOK® (HITS PLAN, Tokyo, Japan); IllumiScan® (SHOFU, Kyoto, Japan)
site_selection_index_test: ROI of lesion defined as area of FVL; control ROI set at normal mucosa in same sub-site, away from lesion without FVL.
technique: Image processing analysis performed on FV images using ImageJ. ROIs for lesion and control area established. VRatio (ratio of lesion G value to normal mucosa control G value) computed. Cut-off set at 87.5%.
positivity_threshold: Cut-off set at VRatio 87.5%; values below cut-off considered positive for oral cancer.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: value ratio (lesion/control G value) below 87.5%
comments_index_test: Objective evaluation sub-arm using value ratio (VRatio). AUC 0.827, sensitivity 85.1%, specificity 75.8%. VRatio corrects for environmental lighting variation using normal mucosa control. Shares patient population with all other evaluation arms.

site_selection_index_test: One oral lesion smear was taken from each patient using a cytobrush all over the lesion
specimen_collection: Cytobrush smear taken from each patient over the lesion and stored in PreservCyt Thinprep; three cytologic slides prepared using Cellspin I semi-automated cytocentrifuge
technique: Slides prepared via Cellspin I semi-automated cytocentrifuge (TharmacGmbH), stained by Papanicolaou, and classified using an adaptation of Remmerbach et al. Results categorised as: insufficient; negative for intraepithelial lesion/malignancy; low-grade lesion; high-grade lesion; suspicious for malignancy; or SCC. Two cytologists performed analyses, compared results, and discussed discrepancies with a third cytologist.
positivity_threshold: High-risk cytologic results: high-grade lesions suspicious for malignancy and squamous cell carcinoma samples
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: high-grade lesion, suspicious for malignancy, or SCC
calibration_of_assessors: Two cytologists performed analyses, compared their results, and discussed discrepancies with a third cytologist.
comments_index_test: 10 cytology samples were inadequate; of 98 patients, 88 had evaluable cytology results (34 low-risk, 54 high-risk). Arm also evaluated separately for high-risk anatomical sites (tongue, floor of mouth).

site_selection_index_test: Same slide as cytology preparation; cytobrush smear taken from the oral lesion
specimen_collection: Same cytobrush smear used for cytology; slides previously stained by Papanicolaou were uncovered and re-stained for DNA-ICM analysis
technique: Slides uncovered in xylene and stained by Feulgen-Schiff method. DNA ploidy analysed using MotiCyte DNA Cytology Work Station with Motic BA410 microscope and Moticam Pro 285A camera. At least 35 normal oral epithelial nuclei used for calibration (CV <5%). Minimum 200 nuclei randomly selected per slide plus morphologically suspicious cells. Results classified as euploid or aneuploid per 4th ESACP Consensus guidelines.
positivity_threshold: Aneuploid if stemline DNA index <0.90 and >1.10 or <1.80 and >2.20 or <3.60 and >4.40 or if there were cells with exceeding 9c content
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: DNA aneuploidy (stemline index outside normal range or cells >9c)
calibration_of_assessors: For calibration reference, at least 35 nuclei of normal oral epithelial cells were selected; coefficient of variation of reference cells of <5% was adopted for quality assurance.
comments_index_test: 15 DNA-ICM samples were inadequate; 83 of 98 patients had evaluable DNA-ICM results. DNA-ICM performed on same slide as cytology (Papanicolaou then Feulgen). Arm also evaluated separately for high-risk anatomical sites (tongue, floor of mouth).

site_selection_index_test: One oral lesion smear taken from each patient using a cytobrush all over the lesion
specimen_collection: Same cytobrush smear used for both cytology and DNA-ICM analysis on the same slide
technique: Both cytology (Papanicolaou stain, classified per Remmerbach adaptation) and DNA-ICM (Feulgen-Schiff, MotiCyte system, 4th ESACP Consensus) performed on the same slide. Combined result positive if both methods positive (both high-risk cytology and aneuploid DNA-ICM).
positivity_threshold: Both methods positive: high-risk cytology result AND aneuploid DNA-ICM result
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: both cytology high-risk and DNA-ICM aneuploid
calibration_of_assessors: Two cytologists performed analyses, compared results, discussed discrepancies with a third cytologist; DNA-ICM calibrated with ≥35 normal epithelial nuclei with CV <5%.
comments_index_test: Combined arm analyzed only in patients with evaluable results from both methods (n=54: 18 both negative, 36 both positive). 44 patients excluded due to inadequate cytology and/or DNA-ICM. Also evaluated separately for high-risk sites (tongue, floor of mouth): sensitivity 88.2%, specificity 100%, Kappa 0.77.

site_selection_index_test: All oral mucosal lesions identified during conventional oral examination were subsequently examined with the VELscope; biopsy site selected based on fluorescence loss, or dictated by clinical examination if VELscope was negative.
technique: Conventional oral examination was performed first. Then VELscope examination was conducted. Greenish fluorescence was considered normal/healthy mucosa. Dark/brownish color fluorescence (FVL) was considered positive for dysplastic changes. Dysplastic tissues with significant keratinization could exhibit increased whiteness with loss of fluorescence around the lesion periphery.
positivity_threshold: Dark/brownish color fluorescence (fluorescence visualization loss, FVL) observed through Velscope was considered as positive for dysplastic changes; lesions rated as malignant or dysplastic only when there was a complete FVL.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence visualization loss (FVL)
calibration_of_assessors: The conventional oral examination was done by trained field investigators; the VELscope examination was performed by dental surgeon/trained Field Investigator at PHCs and CHCs.
comments_index_test: Unit of analysis appears to be lesions (250 lesions from 250 patients — one lesion per patient assumed). The study also evaluated conventional oral examination (white light) as a second index test arm in the same 250 patients/lesions. Twelve cases in white light examination had no result (could not be classified as positive or negative), reducing the WLE contingency table to 238; VELscope contingency table uses all 250. False-positive rate was high (78/114 FVL cases were benign), limiting specificity. No explicit blinding of assessors to histopathology results or clinical information was reported.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Tissue reflectance (White Light Examination / Conventional Oral Examination)
site_selection_index_test: Conventional oral examination of all oral mucosal lesions in all 250 subjects with suspicious oral mucosal lesions.
technique: Conventional oral examination performed under white operatory light at PHCs and CHCs by trained field investigators; a provisional clinical diagnosis was noted. Lesions classified as positive (suspicious) or negative.
positivity_threshold: Lesion classified as positive (suspicious) on white light/conventional oral examination; negative if no suspicious features detected.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: clinically suspicious lesion on white light examination
calibration_of_assessors: The conventional oral examination was done by trained field investigators at PHCs and CHCs.
comments_index_test: 12 of 250 lesions had no result on white light examination (could not be classified positive or negative), so the WLE 2x2 contingency table is based on 238 lesions. The WLE was performed before VELscope in the same patients. Sensitivity 100%, specificity 10.40%, PPV 16.59%, NPV 100%, accuracy 23.95%. Both arms share the same patient/lesion population — paired design.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically visible oral lesions; biopsy taken from stained sites; in non-stained lesions, biopsy site decided clinically.
technique: Patients rinsed mouth with water, then given 1% acetic acid mouthwash for 20 seconds. Then 1% toluidine blue applied to lesion with cotton swab, followed by acetic acid mouthwash to remove excess stain. Staining recorded as positive or negative irrespective of intensity.
positivity_threshold: The staining is recorded as positive or negative irrespective of the intensity of the stain.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: any stain retention regardless of intensity
calibration_of_assessors: All biopsies assessed by two histopathologists independently.
comments_index_test: The study also used 1% acetic acid as a pre-rinse before toluidine blue application and as a post-stain rinse to remove excess dye; acetic acid was not evaluated as a standalone index test. A subgroup of 15 patients with prior surgery/radiotherapy was analysed separately (Tables 5–6). A second analysis excluding cases with epithelial hyperplasia and heavy inflammation was also performed, but results reported narratively only.

site_selection_index_test: Applied directly on the oral leukoplakia lesion on buccal mucosa; all patients presented with lesions on buccal mucosa alone.
technique: Patients rinsed with 1% lactic acid and distilled water for 30 seconds. Target mucosa dried with gauze. 1% MB applied directly on lesion with cotton bud for 30 seconds. Patients rinsed again with 1% lactic acid for 30 seconds to wash out excess dye. Pattern of dye retention assessed by intensity of stain retention.
positivity_threshold: Dark royal blue/deep blue stains of MB were considered as positive retention. Wide, shallow, faint, pale royal blue stains or no retention of the stain were considered as negative for MB retention.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark royal blue/deep blue stain retention
calibration_of_assessors: The interpretation of stains was conducted initially by two examiners (DS, AK) in all the cases. In case of disagreement between the examiners, third examiner (AS) evaluated the lesion and decision was taken in favour of majority opinion.
comments_index_test: Sensitivity 57.82%, specificity 100%, PPV 100%, NPV 26.53%, DA 46%. High false negative rate attributed to inclusion of predominantly homogeneous leukoplakia and strict positivity criterion (pale blue counted as negative). Biopsy site selected based on MB retention; in cases without MB retention, clinical judgement used.

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (Methylene Blue + Lugol's Iodine double staining)
index_test_reagent_name: 1% methylene blue followed by 3% Lugol's iodine
site_selection_index_test: Applied to the lesional and perilesional sites on buccal mucosa; LI applied after MB staining to the same areas.
technique: After MB staining and rinsing (as described for MB arm), 3% LI was applied to the lesional and perilesional sites with a cotton bud for 10–20 seconds. Areas staining dark brown with LI (positive) were considered normal; pale yellow or unstained areas (negative) were considered dysplastic.
positivity_threshold: For MB: dark royal blue/deep blue stain = positive. For LI: pale yellow or unstained = negative (dysplastic); dark brown = positive (normal). Double staining positive for dysplasia = MB positive and LI negative, or MB negative and LI negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: MB stain retention with LI unstained area (pale yellow/no stain)
calibration_of_assessors: The interpretation of stains was conducted initially by two examiners (DS, AK) in all the cases. In case of disagreement between the examiners, third examiner (AS) evaluated the lesion and decision was taken in favour of majority opinion.
comments_index_test: Sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV all 100% with double staining. MB applied first followed by LI in all cases; the reverse order was not evaluated (noted as a study limitation). Abstract states '5% MB and 3% LI' but Methods section describes '1% MB'; concentration discrepancy in the paper. Double staining method not previously studied in oral PMD per authors.

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (Identafi® Violet Light, 405 nm)
site_selection_index_test: All oral mucosal lesions clinically diagnosed as OPMDs were examined; the instrument was switched to violet light for examination of any loss of autofluorescence (LOA) where suspicious lesion will appear dark.
technique: Room and operatory lights were dimmed. Identafi® switched to violet light; lesions displaying LOA were noted. All lesions displaying LOA were blanched to evaluate diascopic fluorescence. Lesions with complete blanching were considered negative; partial blanching considered positive for LOA.
positivity_threshold: Lesions that displayed LOA were considered to be positive and lesions that displayed no LOA or gain of autofluorescence were considered to be negative. Lesions with partial blanching were considered to be positive for LOA.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of autofluorescence (LOA) or partial blanching
comments_index_test: Identafi® violet light (autofluorescence) and green-amber light (reflectance) were applied sequentially to the same 63 lesions in the same patients; arms are not independent. Histopathological reference standard was presence of dysplasia. Sensitivity 73%, specificity 46.2%, p=0.097 (not statistically significant).

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Tissue reflectance (Identafi® Green-Amber Light, 545 nm)
site_selection_index_test: All oral mucosal lesions clinically diagnosed as OPMDs were examined; after violet light assessment, the light was switched to green-amber to visualize vasculature differences between normal and abnormal tissue.
technique: After violet light assessment, Identafi® was switched to green-amber light; examiner directly observed vasculature or arrangement of blood vessels of the abnormal tissue. Diffuse vascularity (appeared darker) was noted as positive.
positivity_threshold: Lesions with diffuse vascularity (appeared darker) were considered to be positive and lesions without visible vasculature or with vasculature similar to the surrounding mucosa were considered to be negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: diffuse vascularity (darker appearance)
comments_index_test: Identafi® green-amber light (reflectance) and violet light (autofluorescence) were applied sequentially to the same 63 lesions; arms share the same patients and are not independent. Sensitivity 78.4%, specificity 15.4%, p=0.389 (not statistically significant).

site_selection_index_test: Applied to OPMDs lesions after screening with Identafi®; clinical photographs taken before and after screening.
technique: Toluidine blue prepared as described by Mashberg. Patients rinsed with water for 20 s. 1% acetic acid applied for 20 s to remove rosy saliva. Area dried with gauze. 1% toluidine blue applied with cotton swab for 1 min. Then 1% acetic acid applied for 1 min. Patients rinsed with water again.
positivity_threshold: Dark blue stain uptake was considered positive. A light blue staining or absence of staining was taken as a negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain retention
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied after Identafi® screening to the same 63 lesions; all three arms share the same patients/lesions and are not independent. Sensitivity 51.4%, specificity 84.6%, p=0.04 (statistically significant). Biopsy site selection used LOA, toluidine blue positivity, and clinical judgment together.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspected oral leukoplakia lesions
technique: TBS applied to lesions; pre and post images taken. Lesions staining positive were re-stained after 2 weeks to lower false positive rate. Results compared to clinical and histopathologic diagnoses.
positivity_threshold: Positive staining (stain retention) observed following TBS application; re-stained after 2 weeks to confirm positivity
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: stain retention
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners were involved in the screening and recruiting of patients, as well as the stain application technique, to prevent bias.
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue applied on day 2 (following day after AA and LIS). Sensitivity 91.59%, specificity 23.33%. All three agents applied to the same 45 patients — arms are not independent.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspected oral leukoplakia lesions
technique: LIS applied to lesions on day 1; pre and post images taken. Lesions staining positive were re-stained after 2 weeks to lower false positive rate. Results compared to clinical and histopathologic diagnoses.
positivity_threshold: Positive staining observed following LIS application; re-stained after 2 weeks to confirm positivity
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: stain retention
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners were involved in the screening and recruiting of patients, as well as the stain application technique, to prevent bias.
comments_index_test: Lugol's iodine applied on day 1 along with AA. Sensitivity 91.59%, specificity 12.22%. All three agents applied to the same 45 patients — arms are not independent. Glycogen levels noted as potentially reduced even in hyperplasia controls, contributing to false positives.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspected oral leukoplakia lesions
technique: AA applied to lesions on day 1; pre and post images taken. Lesions staining positive (acetowhite appearance) were re-stained after 2 weeks to lower false positive rate. Results compared to clinical and histopathologic diagnoses.
positivity_threshold: Acetowhite appearance following acetic acid application indicating dysplasia
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: acetowhite appearance
calibration_of_assessors: The identification of lesion, application, and assessment of the lesion following vital staining were all standardised across all examiners in the study.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Different examiners were involved in the screening and recruiting of patients, as well as the stain application technique, to prevent bias.
comments_index_test: Acetic acid applied on day 1 along with LIS. Sensitivity 58.25%, specificity 34.44%. All three agents applied to the same 45 patients — arms are not independent. Lower sensitivity attributed to keratinized/less keratinized lesion characteristics in study group.

index_test_arm_label: Vital Staining (Toluidine Blue Electrospun Fiber Patch)
index_test_reagent_name: 2% w/v toluidine blue in electrospun PVP (10% w/v) fiber patch
site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspected OPMD lesions and non-healing ulcers >2 weeks without identifiable cause identified during oral examination
technique: 1% acetic acid applied to lesion with cotton tip for 20 s; 2×2 cm electrospun fiber patch containing 2% TB applied to lesion for 20 s; mechanically retained stain removed by applying 1% acetic acid with cotton tip for 20 s; staining color and intensity measured by one oral medicine dentist.
positivity_threshold: Dark royal blue staining considered positive; pale or no staining considered negative
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain retention
blinding_index_test_assessors: The oral pathologist performing histopathological examination was blinded to the tissue staining results; blinding of the oral medicine dentist interpreting TB staining to histopathology results is not reported.
comments_index_test: Novel delivery format: TB delivered via electrospun PVP nanofiber patch rather than conventional rinse or cotton bud application. Each 2×2 cm patch contained 16.8±0.98 µg TB. The study did not compare the electrospun TB patch to standard TB staining protocol. All 36 lesions received biopsy regardless of staining result, allowing full 2×2 contingency table construction.

index_test_reagent_name: 425 nm blue light (autofluorescence, 490–550 nm green channel)
site_selection_index_test: Oral mucosal lesions identified during conventional oral examination under white light; NOM ROIs set at sublingual mucosa, buccal mucosa, transition area from molar attachment gingiva to buccal mucosa, and mucosa on floor of oral cavity.
technique: Lesions photographed using IllumiScan® in a dark room at approximately 30 mm distance. Images transferred to computer and analysed using ImageJ v1.53; each image divided into RGB components; G-image created from green channel; ROI defined in lesion area; FI expressed at 256 levels (0–255); average FI, SD, and CV (SD/average FI × 10) calculated.
positivity_threshold: CV cut-off of 1.70 (for SCC vs. non-SCC/NOM); average FI cut-off of 98.5; SD cut-off of 11.2 (per ROC analysis using Youden index)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: CV ≥ 1.70 (fluorescence intensity coefficient of variation)
comments_index_test: Study uses quantitative image analysis (fluorescence intensity and its CV) rather than subjective visual assessment of FVL. Three metrics evaluated: average FI (AUC 0.72), SD (AUC 0.63), and CV (AUC 0.84). Only CV was independently significant in multivariate analysis. NOM group was significantly younger (median 36 years) than SCC (75) and non-SCC (70) groups, which may confound comparisons. The unit of analysis is patients/cases, not lesions. No blinding or calibration details reported.

index_test_reagent_name: fluorescence light-based handheld device, visible blue light (435–460 nm)
site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspicious OPMDs already identified by conventional oral examination under incandescent operatory light; all participants with suspicious OPMDs underwent fluorescent examination.
technique: OralID emits visible blue light (435–460 nm) directly into the oral cavity; clinician views tissue fluorescence. Oral lesions illuminated bright green or white green were recorded as no OPMDs; those with lack of fluorescence/dark areas, or a combination of bright green/white green and dark areas were recorded as OPMDs.
positivity_threshold: Lack of fluorescence or dark areas, or a combination of bright green/white green fluorescent and dark areas were recorded as OPMDs (positive). Oral lesions illuminated bright green or white green were recorded as no OPMDs (negative).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of fluorescence (dark area) or mixed fluorescence pattern
blinding_index_test_assessors: Not blinded; the same clinician performed both conventional and fluorescent oral examinations.
blinding_index_test_examiner: Not blinded to clinical information; the same highly trained HIV-dental care provider performed both conventional and fluorescent oral examinations, and recorded demographic and clinical details at baseline.
comments_index_test: Single-arm study; the same clinician performed both conventional oral examination and fluorescent examination, introducing potential report bias. Unit of analysis is lesions (44 lesions from 44 patients). Biopsy was only performed on unresolved suspicious OPMDs at 15-day follow-up; lesions that resolved spontaneously were classified by clinical impression only, which may affect reference standard completeness. High false positive rate (72%) noted, likely related to HIV-associated oral lesions mimicking OPMDs under autofluorescence.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to clinically suspicious oral lesions identified on conventional oral examination
technique: After COE, autofluorescence visualization (AFV) was performed using handheld VELscope. Findings were categorized as: AFL (loss of fluorescence) or AFR (retained or no loss of fluorescence) as determined by manufacturer's literature.
positivity_threshold: AFL: Loss of fluorescence (autofluorescence loss) classified as positive for dysplasia/malignancy
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: autofluorescence loss
blinding_index_test_assessors: The histopathologist was blinded to VELscope findings; blinding of VELscope examiner to histopathology not explicitly stated.
comments_index_test: Study reports two analyses: (1) all dysplasia/malignancy vs. no dysplasia (sensitivity 77.77%, specificity 25%); (2) high-risk (moderate/severe dysplasia or OSCC) vs. low-risk (no/mild dysplasia) (sensitivity 90.47%, specificity 44.44%). Both analyses pertain to the single VELscope arm. Unit of analysis is patients (n=30). The VELscope examiner blinding to reference standard is not explicitly reported.

site_selection_index_test: Applied directly to the oral lesion (white or red and white oral lesions suspicious of PMD).
technique: Patients rinsed mouths with clean water; lesions were dried with gauze and photographed. 5% acetic acid was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds. A photograph was taken following application and the lesion was observed for colour changes.
positivity_threshold: The results of the acetic acid application were considered positive if the lesion appears opaque white (acetowhite) and negative if the lesion does not show any colour change.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: acetowhite (opaque white) appearance
calibration_of_assessors: The clinical diagnosis was confirmed by an oral medicine specialist with more than 10 years' experience.
comments_index_test: Acetic acid was applied first, followed by toluidine blue on the same lesion, so the two tests were applied sequentially to the same patients/lesions. Single examiner performed all observations; subjectivity in visual examination not investigated.

site_selection_index_test: Applied directly to the oral lesion (white or red and white oral lesions suspicious of PMD); biopsy site selected based on clinical appearance and dye retention.
technique: After acetic acid application, 1% toluidine blue was applied to the lesion with a sterile disposable cotton applicator for 60 seconds and decolorized with acetic acid. A photograph of the lesion was taken following this procedure.
positivity_threshold: The lesion was considered toluidine blue positive if it retained blue colour after the staining. Lesions with no uptake or questionable uptake constituted the negative toluidine blue category.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: blue colour retention after decolorization
calibration_of_assessors: The clinical diagnosis was confirmed by an oral medicine specialist with more than 10 years' experience.
comments_index_test: Toluidine blue was applied after acetic acid on the same lesions (sequential application); decolorization step used acetic acid. Questionable uptake was classified as negative, which likely improved specificity. Single examiner performed all observations.

site_selection_index_test: All patients diagnosed with OPMDs underwent oral examination using the Velscope device; lesions distributed across left buccal mucosa, right buccal mucosa, labial mucosa, lip, tongue, and buccal vestibule.
technique: Examinations were conducted in a dark room, with patients wearing special glasses provided in the Velscope kit. A blue light (400–460 nm) was directed onto the oral tissues, and the emitted fluorescence was assessed visually. Initially, 10 patients were examined to calibrate the visualization of colours for consistent assessment across the study. Lesions exhibiting loss of autofluorescence (FVL) appeared as dark areas, suggesting dysplasia.
positivity_threshold: Lesions exhibiting loss of autofluorescence (FVL) appeared as dark areas, suggesting dysplasia.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of fluorescence (dark areas)
calibration_of_assessors: Initially, 10 patients were examined to calibrate the visualization of colours for consistent assessment across the study.
comments_index_test: Single-arm study; Velscope used as adjunct to incisional biopsy (reference standard). Cohen's kappa reported as 0.381 in abstract/results text but as 0.581 in Table 3 — inconsistency noted. Sensitivity 88.89%, specificity 46.15%, PPV 77.42%, NPV 66.67%, accuracy 75.0%, AUC 0.675. Small convenience sample from a single screening camp limits generalisability.

site_selection_index_test: Participants were screened for oral mucosal lesions, and those lesions were subjected to DrOroscope examination focusing on identifying dysplastic lesions.
technique: On blue light exposure, the normal tissues reflect green fluorescence, and there is a loss of fluorescence in abnormal tissues, due to which the areas appear dark. The pictures were captured with the image sensor. Image analysis was done using software algorithms generated from AI concepts. After a thorough image analysis by DrOroscope, the lesions were categorized into variable, borderline, and severe.
positivity_threshold: Loss of fluorescence on blue light exposure; lesions categorized as variable (no dysplastic changes), borderline (mild and moderate dysplastic changes), or severe/dysplasia (severe cases).
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: loss of fluorescence (dark area on blue light exposure)
calibration_of_assessors: The examiner was trained in the operation of DrOroscope and interpreting its results.
comments_index_test: DrOroscope is a novel intraoral autofluorescence device using blue light (400–460 nm) with AI-based image analysis. Unit of analysis appears to be patients (n=40). The device categorizes lesions into variable/borderline/dysplasia; positivity for presence/absence of dysplasia was defined as borderline or dysplasia category. Blinding of assessors to reference standard and clinical information not reported. Small sample size noted as limitation by authors.

site_selection_index_test: Whole oral cavity examined by experienced senior oral maxillofacial surgeons; lesions assessed included leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, and possibly oral cancer.
technique: Visual inspection and palpation of the whole oral cavity for ulcerations, nodules, swelling, or alterations in color and texture; palpation of facial bones and soft tissues to note asymmetries, masses, and lymphadenopathy.
positivity_threshold: Leukoplakia, erythro leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, or possible oral cancer identified as abnormal findings
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: abnormal VOE finding (leukoplakia, erythroplakia, verrucous hyperplasia, or possible oral cancer)
calibration_of_assessors: No significant difference of the VOE judgment among the participated OMS from the three study sites was reported; no explicit pre-study calibration described.
comments_index_test: VOE performed by experienced senior oral maxillofacial surgeons at three teaching hospitals. Used as one arm in a multi-arm study also evaluating ZNF582 methylation. Various logistic regression models (VOE only, MET only, triage, co-testing) were compared. Unit of analysis is patients.

index_test_reagent_name: ZNF582 DNA methylation (quantitative methylation-specific PCR, TaqMan-based technology)
index_test_commercial_name: Epigene ZNF582 DNA Detection Kit (iStat Biomedical Co., Ltd., New Taipei City, Taiwan; CE-IVD)
site_selection_index_test: Oral exfoliated cell specimen collected from the mucosal lesion of each patient.
specimen_collection: Oral epithelial cells collected using a foam brush and preserved in 'Epigene' Specimen Collection and Transfer Tube.
technique: OECs collected by foam brush; gDNA extracted with 'Epigene' Nucleic Acid Extraction kit; concentration quantified by NanoDrop 2000c; bisulfite conversion with 'Epigene' Bisulfite Conversion Kit (converts unmethylated cytosine to uracil); ZNF582m levels quantified by TaqMan qMSP on LightCycler LC480; two Cp values (ZNF582 and COL2A internal reference) used to qualitatively determine methylation status per manufacturer's instructions.
positivity_threshold: Qualitatively determined as positive or negative in accordance with manufacturer's instructions based on two Cp values (ZNF582 and COL2A)
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: ZNF582 methylation detected per manufacturer's criteria
comments_index_test: ZNF582 methylation is a CE-IVD molecular test, not a conventional staining or optical test — classified as 'other'. Used as one arm in a multi-arm study alongside VOE. Logistic regression models evaluated VOE alone, ZNF582m alone (MET model), triage (sequential: ZNF582m only in VOE-abnormal patients), and co-testing (parallel: both in all patients). Unit of analysis is patients.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to suspicious oral mucosal lesions (oral leukoplakia, oral lichen planus, oral submucous fibrosis) clinically identified by the principal investigator.
technique: VELscope examination performed from approximately 3–4 inches distance; nature of tissue fluorescence noted as fluorescence retention or loss; photographs of fluorescence recorded for documentation.
positivity_threshold: Fluorescence loss (FVL) — area appears dark — considered positive; fluorescence retention (FVR) — pale green — considered normal.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: fluorescence loss
calibration_of_assessors: A separate investigator (not the principal investigator) performed the VELscope examination to minimize risk of bias; no formal calibration exercise described.
blinding_index_test_examiner: A different investigator performed VELscope examination from the one who conducted clinical evaluation, to minimize bias; no explicit statement of blinding to clinical information.
comments_index_test: Study evaluates VELscope across three separate OPMD subgroups (OL, OLP, OSMF) each n=10; results reported separately per lesion type. All 30 patients received all four index tests (VELscope + 3 vital stains), so arms are not independent. Unit of analysis appears to be one lesion per patient.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to the suspicious area of clinically diagnosed OPMDs (oral leukoplakia, oral lichen planus, oral submucous fibrosis).
technique: Stain applied to suspicious area; dark blue (royal or navy) stain of entire or part of lesion considered positive; lack of colour absorption considered negative; light/pale blue staining considered doubtful. Doubtful lesions wiped with cotton swab dipped in 1% acetic acid — disappearance indicates negative, persistence indicates biopsy.
positivity_threshold: A dark blue (royal or navy) stain of either the entire lesion or a portion of it was considered positive; lack of colour absorption as negative; light or pale blue staining as doubtful.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: dark blue stain retention
comments_index_test: All 30 patients received all four index tests (VELscope + 3 vital stains); arms not independent. Results reported separately for OL (n=10), OLP (n=10), OSMF (n=10). Concentration of toluidine blue solution not explicitly stated.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to the suspicious area of clinically diagnosed OPMDs (oral leukoplakia, oral lichen planus, oral submucous fibrosis).
technique: Stain applied to suspicious area; deep blue stains that were local, stippled and patchy considered positive; faint blue stains that were wide, shallow and easily washable considered negative.
positivity_threshold: Deep blue stains, which were local, stippled and patchy were considered to be positive; faint blue stains, which were wide, shallow and easily washable, were considered negative.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: deep blue stain retention (local, stippled, patchy)
comments_index_test: All 30 patients received all four index tests; arms not independent. Results reported separately for OL (n=10), OLP (n=10), OSMF (n=10). Concentration of methylene blue solution not explicitly stated.

site_selection_index_test: Applied to the suspicious area of clinically diagnosed OPMDs (oral leukoplakia, oral lichen planus, oral submucous fibrosis).
technique: Stain applied to suspicious area; malignant/dysplastic tissues with reduced glycogen content remain unstained, while normal epithelium stains brown or black. Uptake of stain considered positive; no uptake or light uptake considered negative.
positivity_threshold: Uptake of stain considered positive for dysplasia; no uptake or light uptake of staining considered negative. Malignant/dysplastic tissue remains unstained (positive finding) while normal epithelium stains brown or black.
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: unstained area (absent iodine uptake)
comments_index_test: All 30 patients received all four index tests; arms not independent. Results reported separately for OL (n=10), OLP (n=10), OSMF (n=10). Concentration of Lugol's iodine not explicitly stated. Note: for Lugol's iodine, positive = unstained (unlike toluidine blue/methylene blue where positive = stained).

index_test_arm_label: Light-based test - Autofluorescence (Multispectral Autofluorescence Imaging Endoscopy)
index_test_reagent_name: 355 nm pulsed laser; emission bands at 390 ± 20 nm, 452 ± 22.5 nm, and >500 nm
site_selection_index_test: Suspicious oral lesion and a clinically healthy-appearing area in the corresponding contralateral anatomical side
technique: In vivo multispectral autofluorescence endoscopic images acquired with 10 mm circular field-of-view, ~100 μm lateral resolution, <3 s acquisition time per multispectral image, using 355 nm pulsed laser collecting emission at 390 ± 20 nm, 452 ± 22.5 nm, and >500 nm bands. Images preprocessed by subtracting signal offset/background, masking saturated pixels, applying 5×5 spatial averaging filter, masking low-SNR pixels, and manually masking teeth regions.
positivity_threshold: Image-level score (average of posterior probability map) greater than or equal to an optimized threshold selected from ROC curve with maximum sensitivity within 1-specificity range of 0% to 30%
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: image-level score ≥ optimized ROC-derived threshold
blinding_index_test_assessors: An incisional tissue biopsy was then taken from the center of the lesion, which was blinded to the autofluorescence endoscopy imaging acquisition and processing.
comments_index_test: Study uses machine learning (L1-SVM) classification rather than human visual interpretation; positivity threshold is algorithm-derived. Two model arms evaluated: (1) optimal multispectral L1-SVM with top four features (sensitivity 85%, specificity 71%) and (2) single-feature model simulating VELscope (sensitivity 61%, specificity 71%). Both arms share the same patient cohort. The reference standard (histopathology) was blinded to imaging acquisition/processing. Unit of analysis is lesions (one per patient).

index_test_reagent_name: Single spectral feature: combined normalized autofluorescence intensities at 452 ± 22.5 nm and >500 nm emission bands (I452,n + I500,n)
site_selection_index_test: Suspicious oral lesion and a clinically healthy-appearing area in the corresponding contralateral anatomical side
technique: Same image acquisition as multispectral arm; classification uses only combined normalized autofluorescence intensities at 452 ± 22.5 nm and >500 nm bands (I452,n + I500,n) as a single feature in an L1-SVM model, simulating the VELscope single-emission-band approach.
positivity_threshold: Image-level score (average of posterior probability map) greater than or equal to an optimized threshold selected from ROC curve with maximum sensitivity within 1-specificity range of 0% to 30%
positivity_threshold_transformed: positive: image-level score ≥ optimized ROC-derived threshold
blinding_index_test_assessors: An incisional tissue biopsy was then taken from the center of the lesion, which was blinded to the autofluorescence endoscopy imaging acquisition and processing.
comments_index_test: This arm is a comparator model simulating the VELscope device, not an actual VELscope measurement; it uses the same imaging data as the multispectral arm but restricts classification to a single combined feature. Sensitivity 61%, specificity 71%, accuracy 66%. Shares the same patient cohort as the multispectral arm — results are not independent.
